identity.title: Statistical Efficiency of Distributional Temporal Difference Learning

problem.claim: Analyze finite-sample performance for distributional policy evaluation using distributional temporal-difference learning in tabular discounted MDPs.

gap.claim: Earlier cited results established asymptotic convergence for CTD and QTD, leaving finite-sample performance as the next analysis target.

contributions.claim: Proposes non-parametric distributional TD learning (NTD) to facilitate theoretical analysis.
Establishes a novel Freedman inequality in Hilbert spaces for the analysis.
Revisits CTD and reports matching non-asymptotic convergence bounds under p-Wasserstein error.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present NTD, a Hilbert-space Freedman inequality, and a finite-sample analysis extending prior asymptotic results.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that NTD requires \widetilde O(1/[ε^{2p}(1−γ)^{2p+1}]) iterations to obtain an ε-optimal estimator with high probability under p-Wasserstein error.
The authors report that this sample-complexity bound is minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors for 1-Wasserstein distance.
The authors report that CTD satisfies the same non-asymptotic convergence bounds in p-Wasserstein distance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Distributional policy evaluation estimates a policy’s return distribution, and distributional TD extends classic TD to this task.
Prior cited tabular analyses proved asymptotic convergence for CTD and QTD; the paper targets finite-sample performance.
The paper introduces NTD and a Hilbert-space Freedman inequality to support the theoretical analysis.
For discounted infinite-horizon tabular MDPs, the authors report p-Wasserstein sample-complexity bounds for NTD, minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors at p=1, and matching bounds for CTD.

source_observation.claim: The abstract states the estimator’s rate together with its error metric, discount-factor dependence, probability qualifier, and a restricted minimax-optimality claim for p=1.

lessons.interpretation: A theoretical abstract becomes more decision-useful when rate, metric, conditions, and scope of optimality are stated together.
lessons.application: When presenting a learning-theoretic result, report the complexity scaling alongside the metric, environmental assumptions, probability guarantee, and exact regime of any optimality comparison.
lessons.exception: This format may be unsuitable when the result is primarily qualitative or when the relevant assumptions cannot be compressed without becoming misleading.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify NTD’s update rule, estimator construction, confidence dependence, state/action-size dependence, or constants.
The abstract states that CTD has the same reported p-Wasserstein convergence bounds as NTD, but does not detail the assumptions or derivation needed to obtain them.
The abstract does not provide proof details for the Hilbert-space inequality or the minimax lower bound.

editorial_revisions.before: The precise conditions and meaning of “same” CTD bounds are not given.
editorial_revisions.after: The abstract states that CTD has the same reported p-Wasserstein convergence bounds as NTD, but does not detail the assumptions or derivation needed to obtain them.
